name: Business setup and PRO services (UAE)

problems.words: Leads come from ads and WhatsApp, and half never get a reply the same day
quick_ideas: Reply today to every enquiry still waiting, so warm leads aren't lost
Name one person who owns new enquiries each day, so replies stop depending on who looks.

workzap_build.text: one lead inbox for website, ads and WhatsApp with assignment, a reply timer and reminders until contact is made.

problems.ask_first: Where do most of your leads come from?
problems.free_stops: assignment rules and reply timings are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count today's enquiries that waited past closing without a reply, so you see how much same day response is slipping.
Set one midday and one late afternoon check for all new enquiries, so replies reach leads while interest is fresh.

problems.words: We spend on Google ads and can't tell which leads became clients
quick_ideas: Ask every new lead where they found you, so you start recording source
Mark the source on this month's won clients once, so you get a first picture.

workzap_build.text: tracked links and codes per ad and channel, so every client shows which campaign brought them.

problems.ask_first: Do most of your new leads come from Google ads, or do the ads bring only a few?
problems.free_stops: how tracking is set up for your campaigns is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark this month's client companies against the lead source already noted in chats, so you see which enquiries actually turned into work.
Give one person the job of noting source beside each new client company, so ad spending links back to signed work.

problems.words: Quotations are made in Word and every consultant prices differently
quick_ideas: Write one standard price list for your main packages, so quotes start from the same base
Agree who approves discounts, so exceptions are controlled.

workzap_build.text: a quotation builder from your price list and package templates, with an approval step for discounts.

problems.ask_first: Do consultants differ mainly on discounts, or on which services they include in the quote?
problems.free_stops: package templates and approval rules are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's quotations for the same service type across consultants, so inconsistent pricing shows up before more quotes go out.
Keep one handwritten master list of current package prices at the quoting desk, so every consultant starts from the same numbers.

problems.words: Clients keep asking "where is my licence?
quick_ideas: Send each active client one update on where their case stands, so the calls ease
Tell new clients once what the main stages are, so they know what to expect.

workzap_build.text: a case tracker with stages for each service, sending clients a WhatsApp update at each stage.

problems.ask_first: Do clients mostly ask about licences that are delayed, or about ones still within the normal time?
problems.free_stops: the stages per service and the update flow are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which active client companies asked for updates more than once this week, so you spot where silence is driving repeat chasing.
Give one person a daily time to send progress notes on active cases, so incoming status calls drop and consultants get time back.

problems.words: Licence and visa expiries slip and clients get fined
quick_ideas: List everything expiring across your managed companies in the next two months, so nothing urgent is missed
Contact those clients this week, so renewals start in time.

workzap_build.text: an expiry calendar for licences, visas, IDs, tenancy registrations and cards across all managed companies, with reminders sent at several points before each date and renewal quotes prepared.

problems.ask_first: Do expiries slip mostly on licences or on visas, and is it a few clients or many?
problems.free_stops: reminder timings and the renewal pipeline are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write every managed company expiry due soon on one page and compare it with who was contacted, so missed follow ups stand out.
Give one staff member the renewal diary and one notebook page for reminders, so expiring cases stop slipping between desks.

problems.words: Government fees we pay don't reconcile with what we billed
quick_ideas: Match last month's government fee payments against client invoices once, so gaps show
Record fees per case from today, so the picture stays clean.

workzap_build.text: a government fee ledger per case, reconciled against client invoices and payments.

problems.ask_first: Do the differences come mostly from fees you forgot to bill, or from fees paid that nobody recorded?
problems.free_stops: how fees are recorded and matched is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each recent authority payment slip with the matching client bill once, so missing charges or mismatches stand out quickly.
Make one person add every authority payment to the case note the same day, so billing has one clean place to check.

problems.words: We pay government fees upfront and clients pay later
quick_ideas: List the fees you've paid but not yet collected, so the size of the gap is clear
Chase the largest this week, so money comes back.

workzap_build.text: client balances per case with fees advanced, invoices and scheduled reminders.

problems.ask_first: Is the money tied up mostly with a few large clients, or spread across many small ones?
problems.free_stops: the collection flow is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many files were paid out before a client company was billed this week, so you see where cash leaves too early.
Keep one notebook page for every out of pocket file and let one person update it before close, so missed recovery follow up drops.

problems.words: PROs run around without a plan and I can't see what they did
quick_ideas: Plan tomorrow's PRO visits on one sheet grouped by location, so trips aren't repeated
Ask PROs for a short end-of-day list of what was done, so you get a record.

workzap_build.text: a PRO day planner grouping visits by location, with check-in and completion notes from phone.

problems.ask_first: Do your PROs lose most time travelling between offices, or waiting in queues at each one?
problems.free_stops: the planning rules and check-in flow are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note today's outside visits and compare them with completed tasks reported back, so you see where movement is not turning into progress.
Give one coordinator the job of writing each PRO's route and end of day outcomes in one notebook, so field work stays trackable.

problems.words: Consultants keep client files on their laptops, and clients leave when they resign
quick_ideas: Move active case files into one shared firm folder, so they stay with the firm
Name a backup consultant per large client, so relationships aren't single-threaded.

workzap_build.text: a client file vault and case history with access by role, so every case stays with the firm.

problems.ask_first: When a consultant leaves, do clients follow within days, or only after a few months?
problems.free_stops: access roles and file structure are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active client companies have updates saved only by one consultant, so the handover risk becomes visible.
Assign one backup owner for each active client company and note it in one team book, so resignations disrupt fewer relationships.

never_say: Any immigration, visa, licensing, legal, corporate tax, VAT or banking advice, or which structure or jurisdiction a client should choose.
Anything involving nominee arrangements to hide ownership, shell companies for concealment, fake tenancy or employment, visa selling or bribery.
That approvals or licences will be issued by a certain date.
Requests for client IDs, passports, licence numbers or bank details.

sample_reply.person: We manage renewals for a lot of companies and every month a few slip and the client gets fined. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this can be sorted, and the first steps are simple.
First, list everything expiring across your managed companies in the next two months, so nothing urgent is missed.
Second, contact those clients this week, so renewals start in time.
For a lasting fix, Workzap could set up: an expiry calendar across every company you manage, with reminders to your team and the client well before each date.

Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
